아브람이 하란을 떠난 지 여러 날, 마침내 가나안 땅 세겜 모레 상수리나: Many days after Abram left Haran, he finally reached the oak of Moreh at Shechem in the land of Canaan.
…Is this the land the LORD said he would show me?
The Canaanites were already living in that land.
여호와께서 아브람에게 나타나 말씀하셨다, 내가 네 자손에게 이 땅을 줄: The LORD appeared to Abram and said, To your offspring I will give this land.
There Abram built an altar to the LORD who had appeared to him.
아브람은 세겜에 오래 머물지 않고, 가나안 산지를 따라 남쪽으로 장막을: Abram did not stay long in Shechem; he moved his tent south along the hill country of Canaan.
그는 다시 벧엘과 아이 사이 산으로 옮겨,: He moved again to the mountain between Bethel and Ai,
and there too he built an altar to the LORD and called on his name.
여호와여—! 말씀하신 대로, 제가 여기까지 왔습니다!: LORD—! As you said, I have come this far!
But before long a severe famine struck the land.
When he came to the edge of Egypt, Abram said to Sarai.
I fear that when the Egyptians see you, they will kill me and let only you live.
청하건대 그대는 내 누이라 하시오. 그래야 내가 그대로 인하여 안전하겠소: Please say that you are my sister, so that it may go well with me because of you.
Abram hid Sarai inside a large chest.
전해오는 이야기는 이렇게 전한다 — 그가 두려워한 것은 사람이 그 아름다: Tradition tells it this way — what he feared was that people would see her beauty.
We must levy duty, so open the chest. Is it grain? Gold? Silk?
Then I will charge you the price of wheat.
…Fine, charge me the price of pepper.
Pepper could not be that heavy. It must be silk.
…(to himself) At this rate he will buy up all of Egypt.
관리가 값을 부를 때마다 아브람은 더 비싼 값을 대신 치르겠다 하였으나,: Every time the official named a price, Abram offered to pay a higher one,
and the more he did, the deeper the official's suspicion grew.
What is in here that he will pay any price? I must open it.
The moment the chest opened, the whole ferry crossing seemed to light up.
…A face like this does not exist in all of Egypt.
관리는 값을 매기는 일도 잊고, 급히 사람을 놓아 바로에게 이 일을 아뢰: The official forgot to set a price and quickly sent a messenger to report the matter to Pharaoh.
애굽에 이르니 바로의 신하들이 사래의 아름다움을 보고 바로에게 고하였고,: When they came to Egypt, Pharaoh's officials saw Sarai's beauty and told Pharaoh,
and Sarai was taken into Pharaoh's palace.
…God, do not let his household fall because of me alone.
I will repay your brother richly. This woman suits my palace.
전해오는 이야기는, 바로가 이때 자기 딸 하갈을 사래의 종으로 딸려 보냈: Tradition tells that at this time Pharaoh sent his own daughter Hagar along as Sarai's servant.
내 딸이 남의 집 안주인 노릇을 하느니, 이 여인의 종이 되는 편이 낫다: Better that my daughter be a servant to this woman than play the mistress in another's house.
…From princess to servant, in a single day.
The LORD struck Pharaoh and his house with great plagues because of Sarai.
이게 대체 무슨 재앙인가! 온 집안이 하루아침에 병들어 쓰러진다!: What plague is this! My whole household falls sick overnight!
바로의 마술사와 점술가들이 재앙의 원인을 찾으려 하였으나 아무도 답하지: Pharaoh's magicians and diviners tried to find the cause of the plagues, but none could answer,
and at last the truth came out.
네가 어찌 나에게 이리하였느냐! 어찌 그가 네 아내라 말하지 아니하였느냐: What is this you have done to me! Why did you not tell me she was your wife!
…I was afraid that in this land they would kill me because of my wife.
어찌 내게 이런 일을 행하였느냐! 자, 네 아내가 여기 있으니 데리고 떠: Why have you done this to me! Here is your wife. Take her and go!
바로는 사람들에게 명하여 아브람을 그 아내와 그 모든 소유와 함께 애굽에: Pharaoh commanded his men, and they sent Abram away from Egypt with his wife and all that he had.
들어올 때는 짐수레 하나가 전부였으나, 나가는 행렬에는 낙타와 가축과 은: When he entered, one baggage cart was all he had, but in the procession leaving were camels, livestock, silver, and gold.
…Will you ask such a thing of me again?
하갈은 사래를 따라 그 집의 종이 되었으니 — 이 여인의 이름은 다음 권: Hagar followed Sarai and became a servant in her household — this woman's name will appear again in the next book.
아브람의 가축과 롯의 가축이 너무 많아, 그 땅이 그 둘을 함께 용납할: Abram's livestock and Lot's livestock were so many that the land could not hold them both together.
Quarreling arose between Abram's herdsmen and Lot's herdsmen.
우리는 한 친족이라. 너와 나, 네 목자와 내 목자가 서로 다투게 하지: We are kinsmen. Let there be no strife between you and me, or between your herdsmen and mine.
네 앞에 온 땅이 있지 아니하냐. 네가 좌하면 나는 우하고, 네가 우하면: Is not the whole land before you? If you go left, I will go right; if you go right, I will go left.
롯이 눈을 들어 요단 온 지역을 바라보니, 물이 넉넉하여 마치 여호와의: Lot lifted his eyes and saw the whole plain of the Jordan, well watered, like the garden of the LORD.
…I will go to that region of the Jordan.
그 땅에는 이미 다른 소문도 함께 돌고 있었다 — 소돔 사람들이 거짓 저: Another rumor already circulated about that land — that the people of Sodom used false scales,
재판관을 매수하며, 나그네를 학대한다는 소문이었다. 롯은 그 소문을 들었: bribed judges, and mistreated strangers. Lot heard that rumor, but chose the abundance of water.
The men of Sodom were wicked, great sinners against the LORD.
전해오는 이야기는 이 대목을 이렇게 풀이한다 — 성경이 롯의 선택 바로: Tradition interprets this passage in this way — it is no accident that Scripture fixes, right after Lot's choice,
\"소돔 사람은 악하여 여호와 앞에 큰 죄인이더라\"를 못박아 둔 것은: "Now the men of Sodom were wicked, great sinners against the LORD,"
롯이 그 사실을 몰랐던 것이 아니라 알고도 물질을 택했음을 일부러 드러내: but deliberately shows that Lot was not ignorant of it; he chose wealth knowing it.
…Go. Live well, for my share as well.
롯이 떠난 후, 여호와께서 아브람에게 말씀하셨다: 눈을 들어 사방을 바라: After Lot left, the LORD said to Abram: Lift up your eyes and look in every direction.
보이는 땅을 내가 너와 네 자손에게 줄 것이니, 네 자손이 땅의 티끌처럼: All the land that you see I will give to you and your offspring, and I will make your offspring like the dust of the earth.
세월이 흘렀다. 우르의 왕은 이제 시날 땅 여러 왕의 우두머리로, 사람들: Years passed. The king of Ur was now the chief of several kings of the land of Shinar, and people called him Amraphel.
전해오는 이야기는 이 아므라벨이 곧 니므롯이라 전한다 —: Tradition tells that this Amraphel is Nimrod himself —
the very king who could not burn Abram in the furnace.
It is the thirteenth year since Sodom and Gomorrah and their three neighboring cities stopped paying tribute.
Your Majesty, King Chedorlaomer has already sought an alliance.
…But Sodom is far, and that alliance is no small matter either.
…Good. We must make an example of the rebels.
I hear that the Hebrew Abram's nephew also lives near Sodom.
…아브람이라면, 폐하의 풀무불에서 살아났다는 그 자 말입니까?: …Abram — do you mean the man who survived Your Majesty's furnace?
Yes. And this time it need not be fire.
…But whether his god can stop swords and spears too remains to be seen.
This time his bloodline will fall into my hands.
그는 옛 원한을 잊은 적이 없었다. 다만 아직 갚을 때가 오지 않았을 뿐: He had never forgotten the old grudge. The time to repay it had simply not yet come.
제6장 · 싯딤 골짜기의 전쟁: Chapter 6 · The War in the Valley of Siddim
그돌라오멜은 십이 년을 자신에게 조공하던 소돔·고모라 등 다섯 성읍이 반: When the five cities of Sodom, Gomorrah, and the others, which had paid him tribute for twelve years, rebelled, Chedorlaomer
gathered the allied kings and came down to the Valley of Siddim.
침략군 선두에는 엘람 왕 그돌라오멜과, 시날 왕 아므라벨 — 옛 우르의: At the head of the invading army stood Chedorlaomer king of Elam, Amraphel king of Shinar — Nimrod of old Ur —
Arioch king of Ellasar, and Tidal king of Goiim.
Those who paid me tribute for twelve years now dare to raise swords at me?
I hear that beyond that valley, near Sodom, lives the nephew of a certain familiar Hebrew.
맞은편에는 소돔 왕 베라를 앞세워, 고모라 왕 비르사와 아드마 왕 시납과: Opposite them, with Bera king of Sodom in front, stood Birsha king of Gomorrah, Shinab king of Admah,
Shemeber king of Zeboiim, and the king of Bela — that is, Zoar.
물러설 곳은 없다. 이 골짜기가 우리 땅이다!: There is nowhere to retreat. This valley is our land!
The trumpets sounded, and the two great armies charged at each other.
한동안은 팽팽했다 — 오히려 소돔 연합이 한 걸음 밀어붙이는 순간도 있었: For a while it was evenly matched — there was even a moment when the Sodom alliance pushed forward a step.
그러나 오래가지 못했다. 그돌라오멜이 다시 밀어붙이자, 소돔 연합의 대열: But it did not last. When Chedorlaomer pressed forward again, the ranks of the Sodom alliance began to waver.
밀리지 마라! 열둘을 조공만으로 다스린 게 아니다!: Do not give ground! I did not rule twelve cities with tribute alone!
소돔 연합의 대열이 무너졌다. 어떤 이는 역청 구덩이에 빠졌고, 나머지는: The ranks of the Sodom alliance collapsed. Some fell into the tar pits, and the rest fled to the hills.
…버틸 수 없다. 흩어져 산으로!: …We cannot hold. Scatter to the hills!
Even in the twelfth year, I am still their master.
아리옥과 디달도 무사했다 — 이 골짜기의 승리는 온전히 그돌라오멜 연합의: Arioch and Tidal were unharmed too — the victory in this valley belonged entirely to Chedorlaomer's alliance.
소돔 왕과 고모라 왕이 패하여 달아나고, 그 대적들이 소돔에 거하던 아브: The kings of Sodom and Gomorrah were defeated and fled, and their enemies plundered Lot, Abram's nephew who lived in Sodom,
and all his goods, and carried them off.
제7장 · 롯 구출 전쟁: Chapter 7 · The War to Rescue Lot
그 대적들이 소돔에 거하던 아브람의 조카 롯과 그 재물을 노략하여 끌고: Their enemies plundered Lot, Abram's nephew who lived in Sodom, and all his goods, and carried them off.
Abram the Hebrew! Your master's nephew Lot has been captured.
Sodom has fallen and all its goods have been taken.
…I cannot leave my nephew like this. I will pursue them at once.
Master, three hundred eighteen men were born in your house and trained.
전해오는 이야기는 이 숫자를 이렇게 풀이한다 —: Tradition interprets this number as follows —
히브리 글자로 \"엘리에셀\"이라는 이름 하나의 값이 삼백십팔이니,: in Hebrew letters the single name "Eliezer" has a value of three hundred eighteen,
so it means that Abram's servant Eliezer alone did the work of three hundred eighteen men.
엘리에셀이 이끄는 자들이 하나둘 모여 섰다 — 대사로만 있던 숫자가, 이: Those led by Eliezer gathered one by one — the number that had only been words was now before his eyes.
아브람은 무리를 둘로 나누어, 자신은 왼쪽에서 엘리에셀은 오른쪽에서, 어: Abram divided his men in two, himself on the left and Eliezer on the right, and under cover of darkness they struck the enemy camp at once.
전해오는 이야기는, 아브람이 흙 한 줌과 지푸라기를 던지자 그것이 칼과: Tradition also says that when Abram threw a handful of dust and straw, it turned into swords and arrows and scattered the enemy.
A few of Chedorlaomer's elite blocked the way, but Abram's blade was faster.
반대편에서는 엘리에셀이, 종 한 사람이라기엔 너무나 많은 몫을 혼자 해내: On the other side, Eliezer was doing, alone, far more than one servant could.
For a moment Eliezer faltered and stepped back.
전해오는 이야기는, 그날 밤 정말로 사실이 된 것은 엘리에셀이었다고 전한: Tradition says that the one who truly became fact that night was Eliezer — wherever he went, the enemy fell back.
The third wave surging in was met by the two, now joined as one.
왕들 가운데 아므라벨 — 니므롯 — 도 있었으나,: Among the kings was Amraphel — Nimrod —
but he slipped away alone under cover of darkness.
His end had not yet come. It would come later, in an entirely different field.
아브람이 빼앗겼던 모든 재물과 그의 조카 롯과 그의 재물과 또 부녀와 백: Abram brought back all the goods that had been taken, and his nephew Lot with his goods, and the women and the people.
Uncle… I knew you would come.
…Was it a wrong land that I chose then?
…The choice was yours. Turning back is yours too.
It is enough that you are safe. Let us go back quickly.
롯을 되찾은 기쁨이 지나가고 나니, 돌아오는 길 내내 두 사람 사이에는: After the joy of recovering Lot had passed, no words passed between the two of them all the way back. Even so, it was good.
아브람이 돌아올 때에, 소돔 왕이 사웨 골짜기 곧 왕의 골짜기로 나와 그: When Abram returned, the king of Sodom came out to meet him in the Valley of Shaveh, that is, the King's Valley.
살렘 왕 멜기세덱이 떡과 포도주를 가지고 나왔으니,: And Melchizedek king of Salem brought out bread and wine;
he was priest of God Most High.
전해오는 이야기는 이 멜기세덱이 곧 노아의 아들 셈이라고 전한다 —: Tradition tells that this Melchizedek is none other than Shem, the son of Noah —
having survived the flood, he is still serving as priest in Salem.
Blessed be Abram by God Most High, maker of heaven and earth.
너희 대적을 네 손에 붙이신 지극히 높으신 하나님을 찬송할지로다!: And blessed be God Most High, who has delivered your enemies into your hand!
전해오는 이야기는, 멜기세덱이 이때 하나님보다 아브람을 먼저 축복하는 말: Tradition also says that at this moment Melchizedek made the slip of blessing Abram before God,
그 때문에 제사장 직분이 훗날 그의 후손에게서 아브람의 자손에게로 옮겨갔: and for that reason the priesthood later passed from his descendants to Abram's descendants.
Abram gave Melchizedek a tenth of all he had gained.
The king of Sodom said to Abram: Give me the people, and take the goods for yourself.
천지의 주재이시요 지극히 높으신 하나님 여호와께 내가 손을 들어 맹세하노: I have lifted my hand to the LORD, God Most High, maker of heaven and earth, and swear—
네게 속한 것은 실 한 오라기나 들메끈 한 가닥도 내가 가지지 아니하리라: that I will not take even a thread or a sandal strap of anything that is yours.
I will not let you say, 'I have made Abram rich.'
제9장 · 언약의 방패: Chapter 9 · The Shield of the Covenant
On the night the war ended, Abram could not sleep.
…아므라벨이 살아 달아났다. 그 동맹이든 그 자손이든, 언젠가 다시 칼을: …Amraphel escaped alive. That alliance, or its descendants, will come back with swords someday.
전해오는 이야기는 이 두려움을 조금 다르게 풀이한다 —: Tradition interprets this fear a little differently —
그가 정말 두려워한 것은 보복이 아니라, 그 밤 자신이 사람을 죽였다는: it says that what he truly feared was not revenge, but the very fact that he had killed men that night.
…I killed men with my own hands. Even if it was a just fight.
You recovered Lot, and that is enough. Rest easy at least tonight.
롯을 구했지만, 그는 내 아들이 아니오. 내게는 여전히 대를 이을 자식이: I rescued Lot, but he is not my son. I still have no child to carry on the line.
…I think about that too, every night.
전쟁에서 이기고 재물을 마다한 사람에게도, 채워지지 않는 것은 그대로 남: Even for one who won a war and refused the spoils, what remained unfilled was still there.
그날 밤, 여호와의 말씀이 다시 아브람에게 임하였다. 그 이야기는 다음: That night, the word of the LORD came to Abram again. That story continues in the next book.
이 후에 여호와의 말씀이 이상 중에 아브람에게 임하여 말씀하셨다: 아브람: After this, the word of the LORD came to Abram in a vision: Do not be afraid, Abram.
I am your shield; your reward shall be very great.
주 여호와여, 무엇을 내게 주시려 하나이까. 나는 자식이 없나이다…: O Lord GOD, what will you give me? I continue childless…
The heir of my house is Eliezer of Damascus.
One born in my house will be my heir.
그 사람이 네 상속자가 아니라, 네 몸에서 날 자가 네 상속자가 될 것이: This man shall not be your heir; your very own son shall be your heir.
Look toward heaven, and number the stars, if you are able to number them. So shall your offspring be.
…If they cannot be counted, I will believe even so, uncounted.
여호와께서 암소와 암염소와 숫양을 삼 년 된 것으로, 산비둘기와 집비둘기: The LORD had him bring a heifer, a female goat, and a ram, each three years old, and a turtledove and a young pigeon,
and had him cut them in two and lay each half opposite the other.
Whenever birds of prey came down on them, Abram drove them away.
전해오는 이야기는 이 솔개들을, 훗날 이 약속을 짓밟으려는 이방 나라들의: Tradition interprets these birds of prey as shadows of the foreign nations that would later try to trample this promise —
아브람이 그것들을 쫓아낸 것처럼, 그의 자손도 매 세대 그 약속을 다시: just as Abram drove them away, his descendants too must keep that promise anew in every generation.
해질 때에 아브람이 깊이 잠들었는데,: As the sun was going down, a deep sleep fell on Abram,
and a terror of great darkness fell upon him.
네 자손이 이방에서 나그네가 되어 그들을 섬기겠고, 그들은 사백 년 동안: Your offspring will be sojourners in a land not theirs and will serve them, and they will be afflicted for four hundred years.
그러나 내가 그 섬기는 나라를 징벌할 것이며, 네 자손은 큰 재물을 이끌: But I will judge the nation they serve, and afterward they shall come out with great possessions.
…Four hundred years. None of my descendants will see all those years.
해가 져서 어두울 때에 연기 나는 화로가 보이며 타는 횃불이 쪼갠 고기: When the sun had gone down and it was dark, a smoking fire pot and a flaming torch passed between the pieces.
그날 여호와께서 아브람과 언약을 세워 말씀하셨다:: On that day the LORD made a covenant with Abram, saying:
To your offspring I give this land, from the river of Egypt to the great river, the river Euphrates.
사래는 아브람에게 자식을 낳아주지 못하였다. 사래에게는 애굽에서 데려온: Sarai had not borne Abram any children. Sarai had an Egyptian maidservant named Hagar.
여호와께서 나의 출산을 허락하지 아니하시니, 원하건대 내 여종에게 들어가: The LORD has kept me from bearing children; go in to my maidservant, I pray.
Perhaps I shall obtain children through her.
When Hagar conceived by Abram, she despised her mistress.
…My mistress cannot bear, but I have borne.
내가 받는 이 모욕은 당신이 받아야 옳도다!: This insult I suffer is yours to bear!
…She is your maidservant; she is in your hand. Do to her as you see fit.
Sarai dealt harshly with Hagar, and Hagar fled from her presence.
여호와의 사자가 광야의 샘물 곁에서 하갈을 만나 말했다:: The angel of the LORD found Hagar by a spring of water in the wilderness and said:
…You are a God who sees me.
Return to your mistress and submit to her.
I will so greatly multiply your offspring that they cannot be numbered.
Call his name Ishmael, because the LORD has listened to your affliction.
하갈은 그 샘을 브엘라해로이 — \"나를 살피시는 살아계신 분의 우물\": Hagar called that spring Beer-lahai-roi — "the well of the Living One who sees me."
전해오는 이야기는, 이 우물이 훗날 이삭이 머물던 곳이자 이스마엘이 다시: Tradition tells that this well would later be where Isaac stayed, and the road by which Ishmael would return to his father's house.
하갈이 아브람에게 아들을 낳으니, 아브람이 그 이름을 이스마엘이라 하였다: Hagar bore Abram a son, and Abram named him Ishmael.
Abram was eighty-six years old then.
제3장 · 이스마엘, 들의 사람: Chapter 3 · Ishmael, Man of the Wild
Years passed, and Ishmael became a boy. He grew up slinging a bow and roaming the wilderness.
저 아이는 장막 안에 오래 있지를 못합니다. 들이 저 아이의 집인가 봅니: That child cannot stay long inside a tent. The wild must be his home.
여호와의 사자가 하갈에게 이미 일러둔 말이 있었다 — 그가 사람 중에 들: The angel of the LORD had already told Hagar — he shall be a wild donkey of a man,
그 손이 모든 사람을 치겠고 모든 사람의 손이 그를 칠 것이며, 그가 모: his hand against everyone and everyone's hand against him, and he shall dwell over against all his kinsmen.
…What do you want to become when you grow up?
I want to be a free man, like my father. One who is bound to no one.
Abram laughed at that answer, but behind the laugh there was a faint worry.
…들에서 사는 것도 나쁘지 않다. 다만 형제를 향해 활을 겨누는 일만은: …Living in the wild is not bad. I only hope he never aims his bow at his brothers.
전해오는 이야기는, 이스마엘이 훗날 다시 아버지의 집으로 돌아와 뉘우쳤다: Tradition tells that Ishmael later returned to his father's house and repented —
훗날 아브라함을 장사할 때 성경이 굳이 \"그의 아들 이삭과 이스마엘이\: when Abraham was buried, that Scripture deliberately notes "his sons Isaac and Ishmael" together
is interpreted as a quiet acknowledgment of that repentance.
Until he was thirteen, Ishmael grew up as Abram's only son.
제4장 · 할례와 새 이름: Chapter 4 · Circumcision and a New Name
아브람의 나이 구십구 세 때에, 여호와께서 그에게 나타나 말씀하셨다:: When Abram was ninety-nine years old, the LORD appeared to him and said:
I am God Almighty; walk before me, and be blameless.
네 이름을 다시는 아브람이라 하지 않고 아브라함이라 할 것이니,: No longer shall your name be called Abram, but your name shall be Abraham,
for I have made you the father of a multitude of nations.
Your wife Sarai shall be called Sarah. She shall be the mother of nations.
너희 중 남자는 다 할례를 받으라. 이것이 나와 너희 사이의 언약의 표징: Every male among you shall be circumcised. This shall be the sign of the covenant between me and you.
…You tell me to mark this old body, so I will do it.
전해오는 이야기는, 아브라함이 왜 하필 아흔아홉이 되어서야 이 명을 받았: Tradition asks why Abraham received this command only when he was ninety-nine —
너무 이른 나이였다면 하루라도 더 빨리 순종할 수 없었음에 아쉬워했을 것: had he been younger, he would have regretted that he could not obey even one day sooner,
이 나이까지 이르러서야 받았기에, 그 순종의 무게가 온전히 그의 것이 되: and because he received it only when he had reached this age, the weight of that obedience became fully his own.
On that very day Abraham was circumcised, along with Ishmael and all the males of his house.
Abraham was ninety-nine then, and Ishmael was thirteen.
하나님이 다시 말씀하셨다: 내가 사라에게 복을 주어 그에게 아들을 낳아: God spoke again: I will bless Sarah and give you a son by her,
and she shall become a mother of nations; kings of peoples shall come from her.
아브라함이 엎드려 웃으며 마음속으로 생각했다:: Abraham fell on his face and laughed, and said to himself:
…백 세 된 사람이 어찌 자식을 낳을까. 사라는 구십 세인데 어찌 낳을까: …Can a man a hundred years old have a child? Can Sarah, who is ninety, bear?
전해오는 이야기는, 아브라함의 이 웃음은 책망받지 않았으나 훗날 사라의: Tradition distinguishes that Abraham's laughter was not rebuked, while Sarah's laughter later was —
because Abraham laughed in joy, but Sarah laughed in doubt.
…I only wish that Ishmael might live before God.
Your wife Sarah shall bear you a son, and you shall call his name Isaac.
I will establish my covenant with him as an everlasting covenant for his offspring.
이스마엘에 대하여는 내가 네 말을 들었으니, 그에게도 복을 주어 그로 번: As for Ishmael, I have heard you; I will bless him and make him fruitful and multiply him greatly,
he shall father twelve princes, and I will make him into a great nation.
…Thank you. You did not forget that child either.
But I will establish my covenant with Isaac, whom Sarah shall bear to you at this time next year.
When God had finished speaking with Abraham, he went up from him.
할례를 받은 지 사흘째 — 전해오는 이야기는 이날이 통증이 가장 심한 날: The third day after the circumcision — tradition says this was the day the pain was worst.
하나님이 그날, 아무 나그네도 지나가지 않도록 태양을 평소보다 뜨겁게 하: It is also said that on that day God made the sun hotter than usual so that no traveler would pass by —
out of consideration, so that the old man would not overexert himself welcoming guests.
But Abraham was rather sorry that no guests came.
…평생 낯선 이를 대접하며 살았는데, 오늘은 그 문 앞이 이토록 비어 있: …All my life I welcomed strangers, and today the place before this door is so empty.
그는 통증 중에도 자리에서 일어나 장막 문에 나와 앉았다. 마므레 상수리: Despite the pain he rose and came to sit at the tent door. It was under the oaks of Mamre, in the heat of midday.
He lifted his eyes and looked down the road for any passing traveler.
And on that day something began to appear before his eyes.
The LORD appeared to Abraham by the oaks of Mamre.
At midday, as he sat at the door of his tent, he lifted up his eyes and saw three men standing there.
전해오는 이야기는 이 셋을 미가엘, 가브리엘, 라파엘이라 전한다 —: Tradition names these three Michael, Gabriel, and Raphael —
미가엘은 이삭의 소식을, 라파엘은 아브라함을 치유하고 롯을 구할 사명을,: Michael bore the news of Isaac, Raphael the mission to heal Abraham and rescue Lot,
and Gabriel the mission to destroy Sodom, it is said.
Abraham ran out himself, in spite of the pain, to meet them.
내 주여, 내가 주께 은혜를 입었사오면,: My lord, if I have found favor in your sight,
do not pass by your servant; rest a little.
아브라함이 급히 사라에게 가서 고운 가루로 떡을 만들게 하고,: Abraham hurried to Sarah and had her make bread of fine flour,
and he meant to slaughter a fat calf and serve it.
전해오는 이야기는, 그가 잡으려던 송아지가 겁을 먹고 달아나 굴속에 숨었: Tradition also says the calf he meant to slaughter took fright, ran off, and hid in a cave,
아브라함이 몸소 그 굴까지 쫓아 들어가 데려왔다고도 전한다 — 손님 대접: and Abraham chased it into that cave himself and brought it back — such was the care he took in welcoming guests.
내년 이맘때 내가 반드시 네게로 돌아오리니, 네 아내 사라에게 아들이 있: At this time next year I will surely return to you, and your wife Sarah shall have a son.
사라가 장막 뒤에서 듣고 속으로 웃으며 생각했다,: Sarah, listening behind the tent, laughed to herself and thought,
I am worn out, and my lord is old; what pleasure could I have?
Is anything too hard for the LORD?
…At this time next year. I will keep that word in my heart.
그 사람들이 소돔을 향하여 일어나니,: When the men rose up to leave toward Sodom,
여호와께서 말씀하셨다: 소돔과 고모라에 대한 부르짖음이 크고 그 죄악이: the LORD said: The outcry against Sodom and Gomorrah is great, and their sin is very grave.
주께서 의인을 악인과 함께 멸하시리이까…: Will you indeed sweep away the righteous with the wicked…
Will you sweep it away even if there are fifty righteous in the city?
…혹 오십 명에서 다섯이 부족하면, 그 다섯 부족함으로 온 성을 멸하시리: …Suppose five of the fifty are lacking; will you destroy the whole city for lack of five?
If I find forty-five there, I will not destroy it.
For the sake of forty I will not destroy it.
So Abraham pleaded, lowering the number to thirty, to twenty, and at last to ten.
For the sake of ten I will not destroy it.
But in that city there were not even ten righteous.
소돔에는 법이 있었다 — 그러나 그 법은 지키기 위한 것이 아니라, 나그: Sodom had laws — but those laws were not for keeping; they were for driving strangers away.
전해오는 이야기는 이 성의 재판관들 이름까지 전한다 —: Tradition even tells the names of the judges of this city —
\"거짓 재판관\", \"악한 자\", \"거짓 증인\", \"굽게 하는: "False Judge," "Wicked One," "False Witness," "Perverter" — their very names were what they did.
The law of this city is clear — whoever lodges a stranger forfeits his property.
굶주려도 죄, 먹여도 죄 — 이게 우리 법 아니냐?: Hungry is a crime, feeding is a crime — isn't that our law?
나그네가 오면 침상에 눕히고, 침상보다 길면 다리를 잘라 맞추고,: When a stranger came, they laid him on a bed; if he was longer than the bed they cut his legs to fit,
침상보다 짧으면 몸을 늘여 맞추었다고 전한다 — 어느 쪽이든 나그네는 살: and if he was shorter they stretched his body to fit, it is told — either way the stranger did not survive.
롯에게는 딸이 있었다. 어느 날 그 딸이 성문 밖에서 굶주려 쓰러진 나그: Lot had a daughter. One day she saw a stranger who had collapsed from hunger outside the city gate,
and each time she went to draw water she secretly hid bread in his clothes and fed him.
…Don't tell anyone. In this city even this is a crime.
…Thank you. I will not forget this kindness.
But it did not last long; she was found out. The judges decided to punish her crime.
She fed the poor — that is her crime. Smear her whole body with honey and set her on the city wall.
이게 죄가 아니면, 대체 뭐가 죄란 말이냐?: If this is not a crime, then what on earth is?
The law is the law, Judge Lot.
벌은 벌을 넘는 잔혹이었다. 전해오는 이야기는 이 일을 하늘이 마침내 지: The punishment was cruelty beyond punishment. Tradition counts this as the moment heaven could no longer bear to watch.
롯은 이 성에 살면서도 그 법에 동의한 적이 없었다. 그러나 성문에 앉아: Though Lot lived in this city, he had never agreed to its laws. Yet he had risen to the seat of judging at the city gate,
and it is also true that he could not withdraw completely.
두 천사가 저녁 때 소돔에 이르니, 롯이 성문에 앉았다가 그들을 보고 일: The two angels came to Sodom in the evening; Lot, sitting in the gate of Sodom, saw them, rose to meet them,
and bowed down with his face to the ground.
The people of the city surrounded Lot's house and threatened him, demanding that the strangers be handed over.
Have you anyone else here? Bring them out of the city.
For we are about to destroy this place.
새벽이 되자 천사가 롯을 재촉하여: 일어나 네 아내와 두 딸을 이끌어 내: When morning dawned, the angels urged Lot: Up! Take your wife and your two daughters.
For they feared he would be swept away in the city's punishment.
…Even so, this city was my home.
롯이 지체하자, 그 사람들이 롯과 그 아내와 두 딸의 손을 잡아 인도하여: But Lot lingered, so the men seized his hand and the hands of his wife and two daughters and brought them outside the city.
도망하여 생명을 구하라. 뒤를 돌아보거나 들에 머물지 말고 산으로 도망하: Flee for your life. Do not look back or stop anywhere in the valley; flee to the hills.
…소알이라는 작은 성까지만 피하게 하소서. 산까지는 이르지 못하고 재앙을: …Let me escape only to that little city called Zoar. I cannot reach the hills before disaster overtakes me.
내가 이 일도 네 소원대로 하리니, 그 성을 멸하지 아니하리라. 그리로: I grant you this request also: I will not overthrow that city. Flee there quickly.
여호와께서 하늘로부터 유황과 불을 소돔과 고모라에 비같이 내리사,: Then the LORD rained on Sodom and Gomorrah sulfur and fire from heaven,
and overthrew those cities and all the plain and all the inhabitants.
Lot's wife looked back, and she became a pillar of salt.
전해오는 이야기는 하필 소금 기둥인 이유를 이렇게 전한다 —: Tradition tells why it was salt in particular —
그 밤 나그네가 찾아왔을 때, 롯의 아내가 이웃에게 소금을 빌리러 보내어: that night, when the strangers came, Lot's wife sent word to the neighbors to borrow salt, hindering the hospitality.
The one who had held back salt to drive strangers away became salt itself.
소알로 피한 롯과 두 딸은 훗날 그 성마저 두려워 산 굴로 들어가 살았다: Lot and his two daughters, who had fled to Zoar, later grew afraid even of that city and went to live in a cave in the hills.
The descendants born of those two daughters later became the ancestors of the Moabites and the Ammonites.
아브라함이 그 아침에 일찍이 일어나 전에 여호와 앞에 섰던 곳에 이르러,: Abraham rose early that morning and went to the place where he had stood before the LORD,
전해오는 이야기는 이 \"일찍이 일어나\"는 말버릇을 눈여겨본다 —: and tradition takes note of this habit of "rising early" —
하갈을 내보낼 때도, 훗날 이삭을 데리고 모리아로 떠날 때도 그는 늘 그: when he sent Hagar away, and later when he left with Isaac for Moriah, he always rose early like that.
기쁜 일이든 견디기 힘든 일이든, 그는 말씀 앞에서 지체한 적이 없었다는: Whether the matter was joyful or hard to bear, he never delayed before the word.
소돔과 고모라와 그 온 들을 향하여 눈을 들어 바라본즉,: He looked toward Sodom and Gomorrah and all the land of the plain,
and saw the smoke of the land going up like the smoke of a kiln.
그 연기는 그가 젊어서 우르에서 보았던 또 다른 불을 떠올리게 했다 —: That smoke recalled another fire he had seen in Ur in his youth — Nimrod's furnace.
그때는 그 자신이 불 속에 던져졌고 살아 나왔다. 오늘은 온 성이 그 불: Then he himself had been thrown into the fire and come out alive. Today a whole city was in that fire, and no one came out.
그러나 하나님이 그 들의 성들을 멸하실 때에 아브라함을 생각하시고,: But when God destroyed the cities of the plain, he remembered Abraham,
and sent Lot out of the midst of the overthrow when he overthrew the cities where Lot had lived.
아브라함이 네겝으로 옮겨가 그랄에 우거하며, 그의 아내 사라를 자기 누이: Abraham journeyed toward the Negeb and lived as a sojourner in Gerar, and said of his wife Sarah, "She is my sister."
그랄 왕 아비멜렉이 사람을 보내어 사라를 데려갔더니,: Abimelech king of Gerar sent and took Sarah,
하나님이 밤에 꿈에 아비멜렉에게 임하여 말씀하셨다:: but God came to Abimelech in a dream by night and said:
네가 데려간 이 여인으로 말미암아 네가 죽을 것이니, 그는 남편이 있는: You are a dead man because of the woman whom you have taken, for she is a man's wife.
…내가 온전한 마음과 깨끗한 손으로 이렇게 하였나이다!: …I did this with a clear conscience and clean hands!
내가 네 마음이 온전함을 알았으므로 너를 막아 내게 범죄하지 않게 하였으: I know that you did this in the integrity of your heart, and I kept you from sinning against me,
전해오는 이야기는, 이 일로 아비멜렉의 온 집 여인들의 태가 닫혀 있었다: Tradition tells that because of this, the wombs of all the women in Abimelech's house had been closed —
사라가 돌아가고 아브라함이 기도한 뒤에야 그 집이 다시 아이를 낳을 수: only after Sarah returned and Abraham prayed could that household bear children again.
아비멜렉이 아침 일찍이 일어나 사라를 아브라함에게 돌려보내고,: Abimelech rose early in the morning and sent Sarah back to Abraham,
and gave him sheep and oxen and servants.
My land is before you; dwell wherever you please.
아비멜렉이 사라에게 은 천 개를 주며 말했다: 이것이 네게 대한 눈가림이: Abimelech gave Sarah a thousand pieces of silver, saying: this will be a covering of the eyes for you,
which proved her innocence before all the people.
…I have put you in such danger once again. I am sorry.
아브라함이 하나님께 기도하자, 하나님이 아비멜렉과 그 아내와 여종들을 치: When Abraham prayed to God, God healed Abimelech, his wife, and his female servants, so that they bore children.
여호와께서 말씀하신 대로 사라를 돌보셨으니, 노년의 아브라함에게 아들을: The LORD visited Sarah as he had said, and she bore a son to Abraham in his old age.
God has made laughter for me; everyone who hears will laugh with me.
전해오는 이야기는, 이웃들이 이 아이가 사라의 친자식이 아니라: Tradition tells that the neighbors whispered that this child was not Sarah's own
주워온 아이라 수군거렸다고 전한다. 아흔 노파가 정말 젖을 물릴 수 있겠: but a foundling. Could a ninety-year-old woman really nurse?
그래서 잔칫날, 사라는 초대받은 귀부인들의 아기들에게까지 자기 젖을 직접: So on the day of the feast, Sarah nursed even the babies of the noble ladies who had been invited —
proving before everyone's eyes that the milk was real.
또한 이삭의 얼굴은 아브라함과 꼭 닮아, 그가 진짜 아들임을 의심하는 자: It is also said that Isaac's face was so like Abraham's that those who doubted he was truly his son soon disappeared.
When the child grew and was weaned, Abraham gave a great feast.
사라가 이스마엘이 이삭을 놀리는 것을 보고 아브라함에게 말했다:: Sarah saw Ishmael mocking Isaac and said to Abraham:
이 여종과 그 아들을 내쫓아 주세요. 이 종의 아들은 내 아들 이삭과 함: Cast out this slave woman and her son; the son of this slave woman shall not be heir with my son Isaac.
전해오는 이야기는, 이스마엘의 \"놀이\"가 단순한 장난이 아니라 활로: Tradition also interprets Ishmael's "play" not as mere mischief, but as the dangerous act of aiming a bow at Isaac.
…The matter was very displeasing to me on account of his son.
Do not be displeased because of the boy or because of your slave woman; listen to Sarah.
The son of the slave woman is also your offspring, and I will make a nation of him.
…I am sorry. My heart toward you will not change because of this.
아브라함이 아침 일찍이 떡과 물 한 가죽부대를 하갈에게 주어, 이스마엘과: Early in the morning Abraham gave Hagar bread and a skin of water and sent her away with Ishmael.
하갈이 나가서 브엘세바 광야를 헤매더니,: Hagar went away and wandered in the wilderness of Beersheba,
and when the water in the skin was gone, she put the child under one of the bushes.
그가 화살 한 바탕쯤 떨어져 마주 앉아,: She went and sat down opposite him about a bowshot away,
saying she could not bear to watch the child die, and she wept aloud.
…How can I watch this child die?
하나님이 그 아이의 소리를 들으셨으므로,: God heard the voice of the boy,
하나님의 사자가 하늘에서부터 하갈을 불러 말했다:: and the angel of God called to Hagar from heaven and said:
What troubles you, Hagar? Fear not.
하나님이 저기 있는 아이의 소리를 들으셨나니, 일어나 아이를 일으켜 네: God has heard the voice of the boy where he is. Up! Lift up the boy and hold him fast with your hand.
I will make him into a great nation.
and she saw a well of water, and she went and filled the skin with water and gave the boy a drink.
전해오는 이야기는, 그 샘이 그 자리에 처음부터 있었다고 전한다 —: Tradition says that the well had been there from the beginning —
하나님이 새로 만드신 것이 아니라, 절망에 가려 보지 못하던 하갈의 눈을: God did not make something new; he only opened Hagar's eyes, which despair had blinded.
하나님이 그 아이와 함께 계시매, 그가 자라며 광야에 거주하여 활 쏘는: God was with the boy, and he grew up and lived in the wilderness and became an expert with the bow.
Tradition tells of the years after Ishmael was grown in this way.
아브라함이 나그네 차림으로 이스마엘의 장막을 찾았다. 이스마엘은 사냥을: Abraham, dressed as a traveler, visited Ishmael's tent. Ishmael was out hunting,
and only his wife was keeping the tent.
I ask for a sip of water and a piece of bread. I have come a long way.
But the wife refused him coldly and turned him away at the door.
노인은 이스마엘이 돌아오면 이렇게 전해 달라 부탁하였다:: The old man asked her to tell Ishmael, when he returned, this:
그대의 아버지가 다녀갔다 전하시오. \"장막 문의 말뚝을 바꾸라\"고 하: Tell him your father came by. Tell him he said, "Change the tent peg at your door."
이스마엘이 돌아와 그 말을 전해 듣고, 아버지의 뜻을 알아차렸다 — 이: When Ishmael returned and heard those words, he understood his father's meaning — to send this wife away.
He divorced her and took a new wife.
얼마 뒤 아브라함이 다시 나그네 차림으로 찾아왔을 때, 이번에는 새 아내: Some time later, when Abraham came again dressed as a traveler, this time the new wife welcomed him gladly
and gave him water and bread without stint.
그대의 남편에게 전하시오. \"이번 장막의 말뚝은 좋다\"고 하더라 전하: Tell your husband. Tell him he said, "This time the tent peg is good."
이스마엘이 돌아와 이번에는 다른 뜻을 알아차렸다 — 아버지가 이 아내를: When Ishmael returned, this time he understood a different meaning — that his father approved of this wife.
Though he was a son who had been driven out, Abraham never let him go completely.
그 때에 아비멜렉과 그 군대 장관 비골이 아브라함에게 와서 말했다:: At that time Abimelech and Phicol the commander of his army came to Abraham and said:
God is with you in all that you do.
그런즉 너는 나와 내 아들과 내 손자에게 거짓되이 행하지 아니하기를,: Now therefore swear to me here by God
that you will not deal falsely with me or with my descendants or my posterity.
…My lord, this man's word is true.
아브라함이 아비멜렉의 종들이 빼앗은 우물에 대하여 그를 책망하니,: Abraham reproved Abimelech about the well that Abimelech's servants had seized,
아비멜렉이 말했다: 누가 그리하였는지 나는 알지 못하며, 너도 내게 알리: and Abimelech said: I do not know who has done this; you did not tell me, and I have not heard of it until today.
아브라함이 양과 소를 가져다가 아비멜렉에게 주고, 두 사람이 서로 언약을: Abraham took sheep and oxen and gave them to Abimelech, and the two of them made a covenant.
Abraham set apart seven ewe lambs, and Abimelech asked what they meant.
당신은 내 손에서 이 암양 새끼 일곱을 받아, 내가 이 우물을 판 증거로: You will take these seven ewe lambs from my hand, that they may be a witness for me that I dug this well.
Because the two of them swore an oath there, the place was called Beersheba.
…The well of the oath. With a name like that, even our descendants will remember it for a long time.
아브라함은 브엘세바에 에셀 나무를 심었다. 이는 단지 그늘을 위한 것만이: Abraham planted a tamarisk tree at Beersheba. It was not only for shade,
but, it is told, his small inn, where he fed and lodged every traveler who passed.
There he called on the name of the LORD, the Everlasting God.
After these things God tested Abraham and called to him.
네 아들, 네가 사랑하는 독자 이삭을 데리고 모리아 땅으로 가서 번제로: Take your son, your only son Isaac, whom you love, and go to the land of Moriah and offer him there as a burnt offering.
Tradition tells that on that road the tempter appeared.
…Where are you hurrying to so fast, old man?
I am on my way to pray.
기도하러 가는 자가 어찌 불과 나무를 손수 지고 가시오?: Why would someone going to pray carry the fire and the wood himself?
…I know it all. You are going to kill the son you had in your old age.
If you kill that child today, tomorrow God will charge you with murder.
노인은 사라지고, 대신 앞을 가로막는 것이 나타났다 — 어디서도 본 적: The old man vanished, and in his place something appeared and blocked the way — a great river such as he had never seen anywhere.
The water rose to his waist, then to his neck.
…Lord, if I drown in this water, how will I carry out your word?
강이 순식간에 말랐다. 시험하는 자는 그 자리를 떠났고, 아브라함과 이삭: The river dried up in an instant. The tempter left that place, and Abraham and Isaac went on their way again.
아브라함이 아침 일찍이 일어나 나귀에 안장을 지우고,: Abraham rose early in the morning, saddled his donkey,
took Isaac and two servants, split the wood for the burnt offering, and set out for Moriah.
전해오는 이야기는, 그 산 위에 오직 아브라함과 이삭에게만 보이는 구름: Tradition tells that on that mountain there was a pillar of cloud visible only to Abraham and Isaac —
a sign that glory rested there. To the two servants it looked like an ordinary mountain.
…너희는 나귀와 함께 여기서 기다리라. 나와 아이는 저기 가서 경배하고: …You stay here with the donkey. The boy and I will go over there and worship, and we will come back to you.
아브라함이 번제 나무를 이삭에게 지우고, 자기는 불과 칼을 손에 들고 둘: Abraham laid the wood of the burnt offering on Isaac, and took the fire and the knife in his own hand, and the two of them went on together.
My father… here are the fire and the wood, but where is the lamb for a burnt offering?
…God will provide for himself the lamb, my son.
And the two of them went on together.
They came to the place of which God had told him.
There Abraham built an altar and laid the wood in order.
전해오는 이야기는, 이삭이 그때 이미 서른일곱 살이었고 스스로 결박당하기: Tradition tells that Isaac was already thirty-seven years old then and asked to be bound himself —
…아버지, 제 손발을 단단히 묶어 주소서. 두려움에 몸부림쳐 흠 있는 제: …Father, bind my hands and feet tightly, so that I do not struggle in fear and become a flawed offering.
Abraham bound Isaac and laid him on the altar, on top of the wood.
아브라함이 손을 내밀어 칼을 잡고 그 아들을 잡으려 하니…: Abraham reached out his hand and took the knife to slaughter his son…
아브라함아 아브라함아! 그 아이에게 네 손을 대지 말라. 아무 일도 그에: Abraham, Abraham! Do not lay your hand on the boy or do anything to him.
네가 네 아들 네 독자까지도 내게 아끼지 아니하였으니,: For you have not withheld your son, your only son, from me,
now I know that you fear God.
아브라함이 눈을 들어 보니 한 숫양이 뒤에 있어 뿔이 수풀에 걸려 있는지: Abraham lifted his eyes and looked, and behold, behind him was a ram caught in a thicket by his horns,
전해오는 이야기는 이 숫양이 세상 창조 엿샛날 해질 무렵, 미리 예비된: and tradition tells that this ram had been prepared in advance at twilight on the sixth day of the world's creation.
He took the ram and offered it as a burnt offering instead of his son.
아브라함이 그 땅 이름을 여호와이레라 하였으니,: Abraham called the name of that place The LORD Will Provide,
as it is said to this day: On the mount of the LORD it shall be provided.
It is also passed down that this mountain is the very place where Solomon, son of David, would later build the temple.
내가 네게 큰 복을 주고 네 씨가 크게 번성하여 하늘의 별과 바닷가의 모: I will surely bless you, and I will multiply your offspring as the stars of heaven and as the sand on the seashore,
천하 만민이 네 씨로 말미암아 복을 받으리니,: and in your offspring all the nations of the earth shall be blessed,
because you have obeyed my voice.
아브라함이 그 종들에게로 돌아가서 함께 떠나 브엘세바에 이르러 거기 거주: Abraham returned to his servants, and they set off together for Beersheba, and Abraham lived there.
Master, news has come from your homeland.
형제 나홀의 아내 밀가가 여덟 아들을 낳았고, 그중 막내 브두엘에게서 딸: Your brother Nahor's wife Milcah has borne eight sons, and to the youngest, Bethuel, a daughter was born.
Her name, they say, is Rebekah.
아브라함은 그 이름을 마음에 담아 두었다. 아직은 그저 먼 친척의 소식일: Abraham kept that name in his heart. For now it was only news of a distant relative.
그러나 훗날, 그 이름은 이삭의 아내가 되어 이 집안의 이야기 속으로 다: But later that name would walk back into the story of this family as Isaac's wife.
Tradition tells of Sarah's last day in this way.
아브라함과 이삭이 모리아산에 오른 사이, 사탄이 노인의 모습으로 사라를: While Abraham and Isaac were climbing Mount Moriah, Satan came to Sarah in the form of an old man.
…소식을 들으셨소? 아브라함이 아들을 데리고 산에 올라 번제로 바쳤다 하: …Have you heard? They say Abraham took his son up the mountain and offered him as a burnt offering.
…내 노년의 웃음이었던 그 아이가…: …That child who was the laughter of my old age…
이삭이 실제로는 살아 돌아오고 있었으나, 그 거짓 소식은 이미 사라의 심: Isaac was actually returning alive, but that false news had already pierced Sarah's heart.
Sarah, unable to bear the shock and grief, breathed her last on the spot.
Sarah lived to be a hundred and twenty-seven years old.
사라가 가나안 땅 헤브론에서 죽자,: When Sarah died at Hebron in the land of Canaan,
…I have come back, Sarah. Too late.
아브라함이 돌아와 그 소식을 듣고, 들어가서 사라를 위하여 슬퍼하며 애통: Abraham came back, heard the news, went in, and mourned and wept for Sarah.
나는 나그네요 우거하는 자로소이다. 청하건대 내게 매장할 소유지를 주어,: I am a stranger and a sojourner among you. Please give me a burial site,
that I may bury my dead out of my sight.
내 주여 내게 들으소서. 그 밭을 내가 당신에게 드리고 그 속의 굴도 내: Hear me, my lord. I give you the field, and I give you the cave that is in it,
in the presence of my people I give it to you; bury your dead.
에브론의 말은 후하게 들렸으나, 그 속에는 값을 더 부풀리려는 셈이 있었: Ephron's words sounded generous, but inside them was a calculation to inflate the price.
당신이 합당히 여기면 청하오니 내 손에서 그 밭 값을 받으소서. 내가 그: If you will, please accept the price of the field from my hand. I will do so and bury my dead there.
…내 주여 내 말을 들으소서. 땅 값은 은 사백 세겔이나 그것이 나와 당: …Hear me, my lord. A piece of land worth four hundred shekels of silver — what is that between you and me?
\"그것이 무슨 문제리이까\" — 겸손을 가장한 말이었으나, 그 값은 결: "What is that between us?" — the words feigned modesty, but the price was by no means small.
It was silver current among the merchants of the day — even at a generous reckoning, a generous price.
전해오는 이야기는 이 대목의 글자 하나까지 눈여겨본다 — 히브리어 본문에: Tradition watches even single letters in this passage — in the Hebrew text, the name "Ephron"
이름이 여기서만 유독 글자 하나(바브)가 빠진 채 적혀 있으니, 돈을 받: is written with a single letter (vav) missing only here, so the rabbinic tradition interprets that after taking the money, even his name
…값을 알면서도 모른 척하는군. 그래도 좋다 — 이 땅만은 누구도 시비: …He knows the price and pretends not to. Still, that is fine — this land must be made certain so that no one can ever dispute it.
…I will weigh it out at that price.
아브라함이 에브론의 말을 따라 헷 족속이 통용하는 상인의 저울로 은 사백: Abraham weighed out to Ephron four hundred shekels of silver, according to the weights current among the merchants of the Hittites.
아브라함이 굳이 값을 다 치른 것은, 훗날 누구도 이 땅에 대해 시비를: Abraham insisted on paying the full price so that no one could dispute this land later — he made it not a gift but a possession.
이렇게 마므레 앞 막벨라에 있는 밭과 그 속의 굴과 그 밭에 둘린 모든: So the field at Machpelah before Mamre, and the cave in it, and all the trees that were in the field,
were made over to Abraham as his possession in the presence of all who went in at the gate of the city.
After this Abraham buried his wife Sarah in the cave of the field.
Isaac, having lost his mother, grieved for a long time.
…In the tent where my mother lived, only her shadow remains now.
이삭은 브엘라헤로이 근처로 옮겨 거하였다 — 하갈이 광야에서 쫓겨났을 때: Isaac moved to live near Beer-lahai-roi — the very well where, when Hagar was driven into the wilderness,
천사를 만나 \"나를 살피시는 하나님\"이라 이름 불렀던 바로 그 우물이: she met an angel and called him "the God who sees me."
…이곳이라면, 버려진 자에게도 하나님이 보고 계셨다는 것을 기억할 수 있: …In a place like this, I can remember that God was watching even over one who had been cast out.
슬픔은 쉬이 가시지 않았다. 그러나 그의 아버지는 아직 할 일이 남아 있: His sorrow did not easily fade. But his father still had work left to do —
제4장 · 이삭의 신부를 구하라: Chapter 4 · Seeking a Bride for Isaac
Abraham was old, well advanced in years, and the LORD had blessed Abraham in all things.
…내가 얼마나 더 볼 수 있을지 모르겠다. 이삭의 짝은, 내 눈으로 보고: …I do not know how much longer I will see. I want to see with my own eyes the one who will be Isaac's partner.
내 집의 오래된 종이여, 청하노니 네 손을 내 허벅지 밑에 넣고 맹세하라: My faithful old servant, I ask you, put your hand under my thigh and swear.
내 아들을 위하여 가나안 족속 중에서 아내를 택하지 말고,: That you will not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites,
but will go to my country and to my kindred and take a wife for my son Isaac.
…혹 여인이 나를 따라 이 땅으로 오려 하지 아니하면, 내가 주인의 아들: …What if the woman is not willing to follow me to this land? Shall I take your son back to the land from which you came?
Take care that you do not take my son back there.
여호와께서 그의 사자를 네 앞서 보내실지라. 네가 거기서 내 아들을 위하: The LORD will send his angel before you, and you shall take a wife for my son from there.
전해오는 이야기는 이 맹세의 방식을 이렇게 풀이한다 —: Tradition explains the manner of this oath in this way —
허벅지 밑에 손을 넣는 것은 곧 할례의 표, 그 언약의 살에 손을 대고: putting a hand under the thigh meant touching the flesh of circumcision, swearing on the flesh of the covenant.
종이 그 주인의 낙타 열 필과 주인의 모든 좋은 것을 가지고, 메소보다미: The servant took ten of his master's camels and all sorts of his master's good things and set out for the city of Nahor in Mesopotamia.
저녁 때 곧 여자들이 물 길으러 나올 때에, 종이 성 밖 우물 곁에 낙타: At evening, the time when women go out to draw water, the servant made his camels kneel outside the city by the well.
…주 나의 주인 아브라함의 하나님이여, 원하건대 오늘 나로 순조롭게 만나: …O LORD, God of my master Abraham, please grant me success today and show steadfast love to my master Abraham.
제가 한 소녀에게 '항아리를 기울여 물을 마시게 하라' 하리니, 그가 ': Let the young woman to whom I say, 'Please let down your jar that I may drink,' and who says, 'Drink, and I will water your camels also' —
let her be the one whom you have appointed for your servant Isaac.
Before he had finished speaking, Rebekah came out with her water jar on her shoulder.
Please give me a little water to drink from your jar.
주여 마시소서. …당신의 낙타를 위하여서도 물을 길어 그것들도 배부르게: Drink, my lord. …I will draw water for your camels also, until they have finished drinking.
리브가가 급히 물동이의 물을 구유에 붓고 다시 길으러 우물로 달려가서 그: Rebekah quickly emptied her jar into the trough and ran again to the well to draw, and she drew for all his camels.
낙타가 마시기를 다 마치자, 그가 금 고리 한 개와 금 손목고리 한 쌍을: When the camels had finished drinking, he took out a gold ring and a pair of gold bracelets and gave them to her.
…Whose daughter are you? Is there room in your father's house for us to lodge?
나는 밀가가 나홀에게서 낳은 아들 브두엘의 딸이니이다. 우리에게 짚과 사: I am the daughter of Bethuel, the son whom Milcah bore to Nahor. We have plenty of straw and fodder, and room to lodge.
리브가에게 오라비가 있어 이름은 라반이라. 라반이 그 누이의 손에 낀 코: Rebekah had a brother whose name was Laban. When Laban saw the ring and the bracelets on his sister's arms,
and heard the words of his sister Rebekah, he ran out to the man.
Come in, O blessed of the LORD. Why do you stand outside?
The servant told in detail why he had come, and Laban and Bethuel answered:

전해오는 이야기에 따르면, 니므롯은 짐승에게 쫓기던 사람들을 구해 낸 뒤: According to the story handed down, after Nimrod rescued people hunted by beasts he became their leader, and he led the gathered crowd to begin raising a tower on the plain of Shinar.

흩어진 사람들 가운데서도 니므롯의 이름만은 지워지지 않았다. 그는 이제: Of all those who were scattered, only Nimrod's name was not erased. Now he meant to raise up not a tower but himself as heaven.
